samples.sample_label: 12-month-ahead I/B/E/S target price forecasts (Table 1; persistence and performance tests)
samples.period_detail: Calendar years 2000–2009; requires 12-month-ahead CRSP prices to measure performance.

sample_unit.quote:
We restrict our sample to 12-month target price forecasts so the one-year period
following a target price forecast release date is our forecast horizon.

sample_period.quote:
Our sample covers 492,647 target prices issued by an average of 2,278
analysts per year over the 10 years, 2000 through 2009
All I/B/E/S target prices issued between January 2000 and December 2009 639,406

data_sources.quote:
We obtain analyst report data from I/B/E/S and stock price and return data from
CRSP.

data_section_full_text:
4.1 Sample selection and descriptive statistics


We obtain analyst report data from I/B/E/S and stock price and return data from
CRSP. Table 1 outlines our sample selection procedures. Our target price sample is
obtained from I/B/E/S’s detailed (stock-split adjusted) price target file. <sup>17</sup> We retain
target prices issued for US firms by identifiable analysts spanning the calendar years
2000 through 2009, which meet certain criteria. <sup>18</sup> First, they must be 12-month

16 Aboody et al. (2010) argue that strong prior returns heighten small investors’ demands immediately
before earnings announcements, leading to post-earnings announcement return reversals. We expect this
effect to also be applicable to the release of analyst reports.

17 ‘‘cumulative factor to adjust stock prices’’ on CRSP to convert stock prices to the same-split adjusted
basis. We use stock-split adjusted target prices on I/B/E/S, so all target prices are based on the same-split
adjusted basis.

18 Our sample starts with year 2000 as I/B/E/S provides target price data from late 1999. Our sample ends
with year 2009, as we require one-year-ahead stock prices data to measure ex post target price
performance.
